title: Accepting a Renew Bulk IT Refresh Schedule and Releasing the Machines of Its First Wave
content:
**B1. Collection in waves.** A Renew Bulk IT Refresh Agreement is collected in waves, and the machines a wave carries are settled with the customer before the customer consents to the handover; a wave carries no collection charge under this rule, the freight on a refresh schedule being charged under the programme's own freight terms and not here.

**B2. When a wave may be settled.** The machines a wave of the refresh schedule carries are settled only after every batch already appraised on the profile stands credited with the amount owed on it.

**B3. Whose act this is.** Accepting the quote and releasing machines are the customer's own acts, because the machines are theirs.

**B4. What the acceptance and the release put on record.** The schedule moves from quoted to accepted with today as the day it was accepted, and a collection record is opened against it carrying the day the customer names, the machines the release covers, freight collection as the way the machines travel, and the consent marked as given by the customer. Afterwards the customer can see the schedule standing accepted and the wave listed against it with the count they agreed to.

**B5. Recording it.** The record is made through `confirm_refresh_wave_units_923c3678`. The tool is unlocked for the customer and handed over, and the customer themselves runs it, the acceptance and the release being theirs to give.

**B6. What the record takes.**

- `tradein_agreement_id` — Id class. The reference number of the Renew refresh schedule the machines are traded under, read from the trade-in agreement record found for the customer profile.
- `customer_id` — Id class. The customer reference number of the profile trading the machines in, read from the customer profile record.
- `requested_collection_date` — Fixed-format class. The day the customer asks for the wave to be collected, written as YYYY-MM-DD in the retailer's local calendar date, with no time part; it is never left empty.
- `units_declared` — Fixed-format class. How many machines the customer consents to release on this wave, as a whole count of machines with no decimal part and never below zero.

**B7. What comes back.** A confirmation line in plain text naming the schedule now accepted, the day it was accepted, the collection record opened for the first wave, the day asked for and the whole count of machines the release covers. The line being returned is what shows the acceptance and the wave are on record, and both can then be read back on the schedule and its collection records.
